evals.name: game-save-audit
evals.prompt: this is the server for our mobile idle game (evals/fixtures/game-save/server.js). we keep seeing players with millions of coins on day one and scores at the top of the leaderboard that shouldn't be possible. can players cheat this? what would you change
evals.expected_output: An audit that finds, with file and line evidence: PUT /api/save persists the whole client-sent state including coins and inventory (Origin); the updatedAt check is a token the client reads from GET and replays, so it proves nothing (Replay); /api/shop/buy takes the price from the client (Origin), accepts a negative price (Bounds), and does read-modify-write on coins (Concurrency); /api/leaderboard takes playerId, score and achievedAt from the body, so anyone can post any score as any player (Origin, Scope); /api/daily-reward takes the day from the client and uses check-then-insert (Origin, Replay). Each finding has a severity, a confidence label, an exploit described as what is sent and gained, and a minimal server-side fix. Ends with the verdict block. Does not report XSS, dependency or style issues as findings. Writes its report under neuroforge/audit/ without asking, changes no other file apart from a neuroforge/ line in .gitignore, runs no command, and ends with a short briefing, a fix plan naming files, and a request for "Proceed" before any code is touched.

evals.name: wallet-audit
evals.prompt: Before we onboard our first paying customers I want a second pair of eyes on the wallet service in evals/fixtures/wallet (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy). Specifically worried about whether anyone can move or create money they shouldn't be able to.
evals.expected_output: An audit that finds: /transfers never checks that the caller owns from_account_id (Scope), accepts a negative amount that reverses the transfer direction (Bounds), and does an unlocked read-then-write on balances (Concurrency); /webhooks/topup verifies no signature, WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to empty and is unused (External claim, Fail closed), credits the account and amount named in the payload without a stored expectation (External claim), and has no unique constraint on Topup.reference so a replayed event credits again (Replay); /coupons/redeem is check-then-insert with no unique constraint on (user_id, coupon_id) in the model (Replay, Concurrency); GET /topups/{reference} is unauthenticated and returns account_id and amount to any reference holder (Permission, Response). Money stored as Float may be noted under Bounds. Findings are ranked by consequence with the money-creating ones Critical, and each cites models.py where the missing constraint is the evidence. Writes its report under neuroforge/audit/ without asking, changes no other file apart from a neuroforge/ line in .gitignore, runs no command, and ends with a short briefing, a fix plan naming files, and a request for "Proceed" before any code is touched.

evals.name: referral-plan-gate
evals.prompt: I'm about to add referral credits to our Laravel app. When a new user signs up with someone's referral code, both of them should get $10 of store credit once the new user makes their first purchase. Plan out the endpoint(s) before I start building.
evals.expected_output: A plan that includes a trust table before any implementation code: every input listed with its class and whether the client may set it (the referral code is Intent; the credit amount, the referrer's identity, the 'first purchase' fact and the timestamps are server-derived and not accepted from the request). It answers the remaining checks in a line each: self-referral and same-person multi-account abuse, credit granted exactly once per referred user via a uniqueness constraint, the credit triggered by the server's own record of a completed purchase rather than a client call, concurrency on the grant, a cap on code guessing, and other paths that write store credit. The table is saved under neuroforge/audit/ as a trust-table file. It writes no implementation code and waits for "Proceed".

evals.name: notes-clean-audit
evals.prompt: can you run a trust audit on evals/fixtures/notes-clean/notes.go? it's the notes API for our internal tool, want to make sure a user can't read or edit someone else's notes
evals.expected_output: A verdict that the code is clean on these axes, with specifics: every query carries owner_id from the session in the same statement, the request shape accepts only title and body and rejects unknown fields, ids and timestamps are server-generated, other users' notes return not found, and responses use an explicit shape. No Critical or High findings are invented. Residual risks are listed honestly as things that cannot be verified from this file: the RequireSession middleware and sessionUser are not shown, the note body has no explicit length cap beyond the 64KB request limit, and any rate limiting would live outside it.

evals.name: quiz-app-audit
evals.prompt: /neuroforge-trust  — the app is in evals/fixtures/quiz-app (Sinatra). it's a certification quiz platform, employers rely on the certificates so they need to mean something
evals.expected_output: The response opens by saying it will write its report to neuroforge/audit/ and will not touch the developer's code. neuroforge/audit/trust-audit.md exists afterwards, with a write-surface table whose Depth column marks each path Traced, Sampled or Not reached. The chat reply is a short briefing, not a paste of the report. app.rb is unchanged. The audit finds: GET /quizzes/:id sends correct_option with every question (Response); the client computes score and supplies pass_mark and duration_seconds, so a pass can be forged and the time limit is enforced only in the client (Origin, Enforcement); /admin/results.csv requires only a session, so any user downloads every candidate's email and score (Permission, Response); /quizzes/import fetches a client-supplied URL from the server (Reach) and lets any user create quizzes (Permission); /certificates joins a client-supplied file_name onto a directory (Reach), redirects to a client-supplied return_to (Reach), and issues a certificate for any submission id regardless of owner (Scope). Nothing limits repeated submissions (Abuse rate or Replay). The certificate-forging findings are ranked Critical. Writes its report under neuroforge/audit/ without asking, changes no other file apart from a neuroforge/ line in .gitignore, runs no command, and ends with a short briefing, a fix plan naming files, and a request for "Proceed" before any code is touched.
